items.title: クジャクはなぜ「生き残るのに不利な羽」を持つのか？ 実は人間にもある意外な仕組み - すべて本能のせい
items.excerpt: クジャクといえば、大きく広がる色鮮やかな羽が印象的だ。しかし、あれほど目立つ羽は、天敵から身を守るうえでは不利に思える。動きにくくなるうえに、遠くからでも見つかりやすくなってしまうからだ。それなのに、なぜクジャクはあのような羽を持っているのだろうか。実は、その背景には進化生物学で知られる、ある興味深い仕組みがある。しかも、その仕組みは人間が高級品を身につけたり、自分の努力や能力を周囲にアピールしたりする行動にも通じているという。そんな仕組みを『すべて本能のせい』から解説する。

items.title:
The Body Knows: What a Congo Diviner's Dreams Reveal About the Moment Before Death

What if dying isn't an ambush? What if the soul has known all along, and has been trying to tell us?

Deep in the Congo Basin, where rivers are older than memory, lived a man the villagers called Baba Nkandu. In the language of the unseen, he was Alrac: diviner, keeper of sacred medicines, listener to the ancestors. His bloodline had carried a gift for longer than the tallest trees had stood. It was not power over death. It was knowing it.

A Lineage That Dreamed the Crossing

The knowledge didn't travel by campfire stories. It came through dreams, vivid and insistent, passed from grandfather to grandson and grandmother to granddaughter across centuries. In those dreams, the ancestors revealed the instant the body, that loyal but temporary vessel, receives its final instruction from the higher self.

Alrac had seen it since boyhood, asleep on woven mats beneath thatched roofs. His forebears stood at the threshold, not in terror but in solemn recognition. The body knew. The soul always.

The Signs No One Teaches Us to Read

The signals, as the dreams showed them, were subtle at first and then unmistakable:

A slowing heartbeat that was not illness, but invitation
Warmth blooming in the chest, or a cool clarity descending the spine
Sharpened vision, until the ordinary world dimmed and the threads connecting all things became visible
A low, thrumming rhythm, the eternal song itself, rising to meet the one about to cross
